source.title: Nonvacuous Generalization Bounds for Deep ( Stochastic ) Neural Networks with Many More Parameters than Training Data

record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own true-label and random-label training and test errors, and compares test errors across fully connected network architectures. These results bear conceptually on V1 and V2, using binary MNIST and a different network family from the versions' cited settings.
record.gate_note: The paper also summarizes Zhang et al.'s results, but those are cited prior work and are not recorded as this study's rows. PAC-Bayes bounds and stochastic-network errors are not rows for these versions because they measure bounds or perturbed classifiers, not the deterministic network behavior named in V1 or V2.
record.test_reason: The study tests V1 in a new setting: fully connected ReLU networks on binary MNIST. The 600-unit architecture fits random labels with 0.007 training error and chance-level test error, while its true-label counterpart generalizes well. The width comparison does not establish V2's zero-training-error threshold or convergence conditions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The central result is nonvacuous bounds for optimized stochastic networks initialized around SGD solutions, rather than bounds directly certifying the original deterministic networks. Deterministic test errors vary little across architectures, and random-label test error is near chance.
record.recipe_differences: Fully connected ReLU networks trained with SGD and momentum on a binary MNIST variant; the study examines PAC-Bayes bounds, rather than reproducing the cited studies' interventions. It reports no explicit regularization in the initial network training.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported true-label test errors vary little across the listed depths and widths; the random-label run required 120 epochs, compared with 20 epochs for true labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Optimized stochastic networks have nonvacuous PAC-Bayes error bounds of 0.161–0.223 on true labels; the random-label bound is vacuous.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: PAC-Bayes optimization can certify nontrivial generalization for stochastic networks around overparameterized SGD solutions on binary MNIST.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix D finds path-norm-based bounds vacuous without strong regularization; strong regularization produces substantial underfitting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The evaluated path-norm bounds fail to certify useful generalization for these binary-MNIST networks.

record.problems: The experiments use only fully connected networks on a binary class variant of MNIST. The random-label run uses a longer training schedule than the true-label runs. Test-error uncertainty is not tabulated; the paper says held-out-data Chernoff bounds are around 0.005 higher.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results were left out. PAC-Bayes bound values and stochastic-network error values in Table 1 were excluded because the versions concern deterministic networks' training and test errors.

untested.parts: The original multiclass datasets and architectures; random-label fitting for architectures other than the 600-unit single-hidden-layer network; coexistence under an identical epoch budget.
Continued test-error reduction beyond an established zero-training-error width, with training to convergence. The single-hidden-layer comparison has nonzero training errors after 20 epochs.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Optimizer comparisons under limited or broader tuning.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps within a convolutional family, including comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Discard the proposed V2 challenge: equal rounded test errors at two widths after fixed training do not establish failure of the claim under its stated conditions. Other true-label architectures provide corroborating natural-label results but lack matched random-label runs.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10, ImageNet, Inception, AlexNet, MLPs on the versions' stated datasets, and multiclass labels; the random-label run used 120 epochs while true-label runs used 20.
Downsampled CIFAR-10 and training explicitly reported as to convergence.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Comparative held-out performance of adaptive optimizers and SGD under tuning.
Comparisons across batch sizes and epoch budgets.
Dropout interventions and their effect on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the training-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

relationships.condition: Single-hidden-layer, 600-unit ReLU network on binary MNIST, using momentum SGD with label-dependent training durations
relationships.reason: R1–R2 report true-label train/test errors of 0.001/0.018; R13–R14 report random-label errors of 0.007/0.508. This demonstrates near-perfect random-label fitting alongside natural-label generalization, with 120 versus 20 epochs.
relationships.display_finding: Natural-label training/test errors were 0.001/0.018 after 20 epochs, versus random-label errors of 0.007/0.508 after 120 epochs.
